definition: For input specifications, these terms define which streams the materials come from, including types of textile waste and other non-textile sources. If more than one source is used, this should be defined separately.
Written name, determined by the actor producing the outputs or the actor buying the inputs
Describes the color of the materials, mostly used for recycling feedstocks.

Name of the desired or in-scope primary textile fiber or other material content (e.g. name of the monomer) according to a standardized list. Fibers that are a contaminant should be listed in Contaminants data fields. In the case that the primary in-scope material content is no longer textile, this data field is simply composition.
% of the total by weight for Fiber Composition 1 Name
Describes how the numeric value in 520.10 should be applied - taken as a minimum, maximum, or absolute value
Describes the functional type of the contaminant.
Describes the material the contaminant is made of.
Numeric quantification of the Contaminant
Unit of measure for numeric quantification of impurity amount or threshold amount (if numerically quantified)
Defines control levels of the contaminant. This is used in a similar way as the threshold for fiber composition to clarify expectations of contaminant control for suppliers or buyers.
Describes if the batch was checked on the presence of a certain contaminant.

For output materials batches, this flags whether the contaminant appears on REACH restriction or candidate list. If this is "yes", SDS and a brief explanation of their use of potential presence in the material batch is required.
Upload SDS for hazardous chemical on REACH restriction or candidate list. Required when Contaminant Hazard is marked "yes".
Brief explanation of use of or contact with hazardous chemical on REACH restriction or candidate list. Required when Contaminant Hazard is marked "yes".
Upload evidence to support claims related to explanation of hazardous substances.
Describes the general shape of the materials to give context to measurements provided in Physical Properties fields.

Describes measurable characteristics that are quantified in additional data fields.
This has a very, very broad application (e.g. fiber length, fabric width, viscosity, brightness)
Numerical value used to measure Physical Property
Unit of the numerical value used for Physical Property Value.
Equipment or testing method used to measure Physical Property

Used to describe finished products (garments and household textiles), some post-industrial waste (cuttings, off-cuts, rolled goods), clippings made during pre-processing, and other formats that include fabric pieces of any size
For use on output batches. This should be determined based on the input materials used.
For use on output batches. This should be determined based on the input materials used.
Quantifies the amount of recycled content by percentage of total weight. If multiple recycled content sources are used, this data should be provided separately in individual lines.
For use on output batches. Should be provided to verify claims about specifications.
